title: Grapevine Winter Driving on I-5: Tejon Pass to Gorman
meta: Winter notes for I-5 from exit 176 to 221: Five Mile Grade, Gorman, Tejon Pass summit, Fort Tejon and listed gas, EV, food and lodging stops along the way.

flags.text: the shutdown usually lasts four to six hours, but some closures run longer than a day.
flags.reason: I did not search for an official source such as Caltrans or CHP, so I could not confirm this typical closure duration or the claim about longer closures.

flags.text: Near the top of Tejon Pass, around exit 204, I-5 reaches 4,144 feet, its highest point in California.
flags.reason: I did not check the elevation figure or the exit number against a primary source such as Caltrans. Tejon Pass is usually given as 4,144 ft, but I did not confirm it.

flags.text: Yes, the Tejon Pass Rest Area is listed at mile 206.1 and serves both directions.
flags.reason: I did not verify that this rest area exists, where it is, or whether it is open. Caltrans rest area status can change.

flags.text: Gas is mapped at exit 202 (Gorman), exit 205 (Frazier Mountain Park Road), exit 215 (Grapevine) and exits 219A and 219B (Laval Road), among others.
flags.reason: I did not verify that these stations exist or that the exit numbers are correct, and businesses at exits change.

flags.text: ice and snow sometimes lead the Highway Patrol to close the freeway between Castaic and Grapevine
flags.reason: I did not confirm the closure authority or the closure extent against CHP or Caltrans sources.

flags.text: On it, the two sides of the freeway trade places, so for about 5 miles traffic keeps to the left.
flags.reason: I could not confirm this claim about the road layout. The Five Mile Grade description and the claim that traffic keeps left are unverified and look doubtful.
